header: SF3 candidate treatment families - comparative/literature evidence ONLY. This does NOT override Baby's direct experimental evidence (SF1/SF2). Verdicts are about whether reference-model design evidence leans for/against each family, not a decision.

candidates.evidence: Granite documents 'maximal update parameterization and a power LR scheduler' (a deliberate non-cosine late-training decay) [DOC]. No reference model in this set uses cosine specifically; Qwen3/LFM2 schedules UNKNOWN. Baby SF2 ran constant LR and swept monotonically past balance (autopsy).
candidates.reason: Confirms LR decay is a legitimate, production-used schedule family and that cosine is only one member; it does NOT establish that annealing fixes a near-boundary miss.
candidates.falsifier_if_adopted: an annealed run that still ends with negative Alex margin on the residual item

candidates.evidence: No reference model freezes/constrains the head during specialization. Granite's constant logit_scale is boundary-neutral (monotone) [INF]. Tied/untied shows no consensus (Granite tied; Qwen3-8B untied; LFM2 appears tied).
candidates.reason: Comparative anatomy gives no support for a head fix; Baby's own component-swap shows the head is only the marginal tipping factor, consistent with 'neutral'.

candidates.evidence: None of the three models documents a token-level pairwise-margin CE objective in base training. LFM2's 'length-normalized preference optimization' is pairwise but in the alignment stage, a different regime [DOC].
candidates.reason: No comparative support or refutation for a margin loss in a small factual fine-tune; Baby's own prior pairwise/discrimination losses failed in the harder binding task.

candidates.evidence: All three models add substantial NEW data between stages (Qwen3 S2 raises STEM/code/reasoning share; Granite 2-stage mixture; LFM2 curriculum data) [DOC].
candidates.reason: The convergent principle is 'continued training should come with a changed/expanded mixture', which argues against simply adding more CE on the identical 16 records.

candidates.evidence: Qwen3's 'thinking-mode fusion' SFT stage explicitly mixes the new-capability data with prior instruction data to retain both behaviors [DOC]; Granite and LFM2 also restructure data mixtures across stages.
candidates.reason: Provides an independent, documented precedent for retention-by-data-mixing in a dedicated stage. Caveat: Baby's Pilot0/1 already showed naive mixing is delicate; and reference mixing is at SFT scale on large data.

candidates.evidence: No reference model uses self-KL to an earlier snapshot. Qwen3/LFM2 use cross-model KD (Qwen3 abstract; LFM2 report) and LFM2 emphasizes 'avoid support mismatch' [DOC].
candidates.reason: No direct analog either way; LFM2's support-mismatch note is a design caution for any future KL placement/strength, not evidence for or against continuing SF2's exact KL.

candidates.evidence: No reference model documents scheduling the strength of a self-distillation/retention term [UNKNOWN/absent].
candidates.reason: No comparative evidence; only Baby's own run informs this.

candidates.evidence: Two candidate ideas surfaced: (a) LFM2 tempered/decoupled top-K KD as a design template for future retention terms [DOC]; (b) a 'dedicated late fusion stage with fixed language fraction' as a structural alternative to interleaving or KL [INF from Qwen3 pattern].
candidates.reason: Both are new framings worth carrying into SF3 design space, clearly labeled as speculation where inference-based.
